IDEAL-001.predicate: Endpoint discovery returns a connectable address, transport kind, and environment override on Linux, macOS, and Windows without treating a marker file as a live socket.
IDEAL-001.reason: Ovis must connect without platform-specific path guessing.

IDEAL-002.predicate: The handshake returns authenticated machine identity, runtime lifetime, control-server boot ID, protocol generation, methods, capabilities, and negotiated limits.
IDEAL-002.reason: A bridge restart must not masquerade as a new terminal lifetime.

IDEAL-003.predicate: An unsupported protocol generation produces `unsupported_generation` before any state-changing request can run.
IDEAL-003.reason: Incompatible peers must fail at a defined boundary.

IDEAL-004.predicate: One established connection accepts concurrent correlated RPCs, subscription changes, and terminal channels until an explicit close or transport failure.
IDEAL-004.reason: Reusing a connection must not discard later requests.

IDEAL-005.predicate: Every accepted RPC request has a unique string ID and receives exactly one terminal result or structured error with that same ID while the connection remains writable.
IDEAL-005.reason: Interleaved traffic must not be mistaken for another call's answer.

IDEAL-006.predicate: Incremental frame decoding produces identical records for every fragmentation or coalescing of valid input bytes, with JSON control and terminal bytes on distinct channels.
IDEAL-006.reason: Socket read boundaries cannot define application messages.

IDEAL-007.predicate: A negotiated frame is at most 16 MiB, and paginated or chunked reads can return at least 64 MiB logical results with explicit total, continuation, and truncation fields.
IDEAL-007.reason: Large reads need bounded transport without silent data loss.

IDEAL-008.predicate: Every malformed method or parameter, including an unknown targeting field, is rejected before dispatch with a stable kind and offending field path.
IDEAL-008.reason: Ignored arguments must never select the focused pane.

IDEAL-009.predicate: Every target-sensitive call requires a typed resource ID or an explicitly requested caller binding, and ambiguous names return structured candidates without acting.
IDEAL-009.reason: Automation must never inherit an unrelated human selection.

IDEAL-010.predicate: Every RPC has a caller-visible deadline, defaulting to 10 seconds, and long-running work returns a queryable operation ID before that deadline.
IDEAL-010.reason: Worktree and remote operations must not hold an ordinary call indefinitely.

IDEAL-011.predicate: Cancellation yields `cancelled_before_commit`, `already_committed` with a receipt, or a queryable pending outcome and never claims to undo committed effects.
IDEAL-011.reason: Disconnect and cancellation must not invite unsafe retries.

IDEAL-012.predicate: Mutations accept an operation ID whose result is retained for the advertised deduplication window, and an expired ID cannot be silently replayed as new work.
IDEAL-012.reason: A lost reply must not duplicate input or resource creation.

IDEAL-013.predicate: Errors contain a stable kind, message, recovery hint, retryability, target identity when known, and an operation ID whenever effects may have begun.
IDEAL-013.reason: Clients need machine-readable recovery rather than prose classification.

IDEAL-014.predicate: Health and status queries return running, stopped, unreachable, or stale-endpoint state without starting, installing, or restarting a runtime.
IDEAL-014.reason: Observing a stopped service must leave it stopped.

IDEAL-015.predicate: Subscription startup returns a subscription ID and snapshot at revision R, followed only by matching changes committed after R.
IDEAL-015.reason: Initial state and subsequent events must have no blind interval.

IDEAL-016.predicate: Every event has one envelope containing schema version, machine and runtime identity, sequence, type, resource IDs, and typed data.
IDEAL-016.reason: Status and lifecycle events must not require unrelated parsers.

IDEAL-017.predicate: State snapshots and events share a monotonic sequence domain per runtime lifetime, and stale snapshot revisions are explicitly distinguishable.
IDEAL-017.reason: A delayed snapshot must not overwrite newer state.

IDEAL-018.predicate: Adding, replacing, or removing a subscription filter is acknowledged with an effective sequence and preserves all unaffected subscriptions.
IDEAL-018.reason: A second subscribe must not kill the first stream.

IDEAL-019.predicate: Reconnect with a retained cursor replays subsequent matching events, otherwise returning `missed` with a fresh snapshot and its sequence.
IDEAL-019.reason: Consumers need deterministic recovery after disconnection.

IDEAL-020.predicate: Each subscription emits a heartbeat within 15 seconds of idle time on every supported transport, carrying its current sequence and runtime identity.
IDEAL-020.reason: An idle terminal must be distinguishable from a dead event path.

IDEAL-021.predicate: Slow subscriptions have advertised queue bounds and receive loss or close state recoverable on reconnect even when the final error frame could not be delivered.
IDEAL-021.reason: A full socket cannot be trusted to carry its own last diagnostic.

IDEAL-022.predicate: Filtering exposes an acknowledged scan cursor, so sequence gaps caused by nonmatching events are distinguishable from delivery loss.
IDEAL-022.reason: A global event counter alone cannot prove loss in a filtered stream.

IDEAL-023.predicate: A complete snapshot includes workspaces, tabs, panes, layout, agents, sessions, terminal generations, geometry, and restoration state at one revision.
IDEAL-023.reason: Ovis must not assemble an apparently atomic roster from unrelated reads.

IDEAL-024.predicate: Every committed create, close, move, layout change, and agent binding change emits a revisioned event naming all affected resources.
IDEAL-024.reason: A mutation must not require clients to invent missing lifecycle notifications.

IDEAL-025.predicate: Completion events carry agent/session identity, turn ID, finish generation, and outcome, with the same values recoverable from snapshots.
IDEAL-025.reason: Replayed or delayed completions must be deduplicable.

IDEAL-026.predicate: A newly registered state wait first evaluates current state and then subscribes atomically, returning immediately when already satisfied.
IDEAL-026.reason: Already-idle or already-exited resources must not cause lost wakeups.

IDEAL-027.predicate: Under the declared local service profile, committed status and lifecycle changes reach a writable subscribed connection within 100 ms without polling.
IDEAL-027.reason: Fast status delivery must be a measured contract rather than an incidental timer result.

IDEAL-028.predicate: Attach returns a structured ready, held, refused, recovering, or ended result, including terminal generation, stream ID, geometry, and reason.
IDEAL-028.reason: Attach control state must not be inferred from terminal text.

IDEAL-029.predicate: Multiple observers attach concurrently without taking input ownership, changing the grid, or displacing an existing viewer.
IDEAL-029.reason: Watching from a phone must not disturb the operator.

IDEAL-030.predicate: A controller lease identifies its owner and generation, and competing acquisition returns a conflict naming that owner without eviction.
IDEAL-030.reason: Input ownership must be explicit and inspectable.

IDEAL-031.predicate: Takeover requires an authorized explicit action against the current lease generation and emits revoked/acquired events naming both owners.
IDEAL-031.reason: A bridge reconnect must not silently seize the terminal.

IDEAL-032.predicate: A late attach starts with a coherent full screen, cursor, terminal modes, grid, history cursor, and output offset before live bytes after that offset.
IDEAL-032.reason: A tail of terminal diffs cannot reconstruct content painted only once.

IDEAL-033.predicate: Attach channels carry only terminal data, while refusal, handoff, takeover, loss, and exit travel as typed control records.
IDEAL-033.reason: Setup noise must never become displayed output or returned input.

IDEAL-034.predicate: Every supported operating system provides direct ordered byte-stream attach, cursor and mode state, resize, and output acknowledgement semantics.
IDEAL-034.reason: Windows mirroring must not remain a lower-fidelity terminal contract.

IDEAL-035.predicate: Screen, history, search, and selection reads neither inject input nor change the application's viewport, and do not refuse an otherwise valid attach.
IDEAL-035.reason: Inspection must not scroll or pause a live application.

IDEAL-036.predicate: Every terminal read returns source, format, content revision, requested and returned range, truncation, completeness, and a reason for unavailable history.
IDEAL-036.reason: A screen snapshot must not be represented as complete application history.

IDEAL-037.predicate: Geometry has a controller lease separate from observation, with explicit release and deterministic transfer among eligible interact clients.
IDEAL-037.reason: A hidden browser viewport must not keep resizing the operator's pane.

IDEAL-038.predicate: A geometry change record precedes output at the new grid, and redraw completion identifies that grid and its revision before input-ready is asserted.
IDEAL-038.reason: Stale-size first paint must not be accepted as current readiness.

IDEAL-039.predicate: Explicit repaint returns a coherent screen at the unchanged grid without fake shrink/restore operations or injected application keys.
IDEAL-039.reason: Recovery must not perturb terminal dimensions to obtain a picture.

IDEAL-040.predicate: Each output subscriber has its own stream identity, byte offset, credit, and bounded backlog; stale or impossible acknowledgements cannot grant credit.
IDEAL-040.reason: One attachment's acknowledgements must not affect another stream.

IDEAL-041.predicate: A stalled viewer is resynchronized with an explicit gap and checkpoint or disconnected, without pausing other viewers or suppressing control input.
IDEAL-041.reason: Slow observation must not freeze an operator's terminal.

IDEAL-042.predicate: Launch accepts explicit executable, argv, cwd, environment, rows, and columns, and reports spawn failure separately from an admitted launch operation.
IDEAL-042.reason: Running a program must not depend on typing a shell command into a detected prompt.

IDEAL-043.predicate: Terminal bytes preserve order and UTF-8 sequences across read boundaries, and the final output offset is delivered before process-exit completion.
IDEAL-043.reason: Final output must not disappear when the child exits quickly.

IDEAL-044.predicate: Input buffering is bounded and separate from resize, cancel, and stop control queues, with overflow rejected before accepting more bytes.
IDEAL-044.reason: A program that does not read stdin must remain controllable.

IDEAL-045.predicate: Pane ID, terminal incarnation, process incarnation, and attach-stream ID are distinct fields, and handoff explicitly states which survived.

IDEAL-046.predicate: Keyboard, mouse, bracketed-paste, alternate-screen, and cursor modes are available as revisioned structured state and drive encoding rather than brand guesses.

IDEAL-047.predicate: The runtime owns authoritative scrollback and exposes revision-guarded search and selection without reconstructing an attached screen from periodic reads.
IDEAL-047.reason: Browser history must not diverge from the live terminal stream.

IDEAL-048.predicate: Input admission atomically checks machine, runtime, pane, terminal, process/session incarnation, readiness, and caller lease against the same target that receives the write.

IDEAL-050.predicate: A submission's text and commit action are atomic relative to other writers, with delivery offsets and partial-write failure reported explicitly.

IDEAL-051.predicate: Send returns admitted or rejected within 100 ms under the local service profile and never waits for the program to become working.

IDEAL-052.predicate: Receipts distinguish queued, PTY-written, agent-accepted, turn-started, and turn-ended, leaving unsupported stages explicitly unknown.

IDEAL-053.predicate: An output wait accepts a previously captured cursor or atomically arms with send, matches retained output since that boundary, and reports an expired cursor as a gap.

IDEAL-054.predicate: Interrupt returns the action delivered and observed process/turn outcome separately, and reports stopped only after matching process-exit or explicit agent-stop evidence.

IDEAL-055.predicate: Disconnect revokes input-ready, and reconnect never automatically resubmits input whose delivery is uncertain.

IDEAL-056.predicate: Blocked input is rejected with a typed reason unless a versioned prompt answer or separately authorized explicit raw interaction applies.
IDEAL-056.reason: Ordinary sends must not accidentally answer an approval dialog.

IDEAL-057.predicate: Prompt events contain prompt ID, version, session/process binding, kind, choices or field schema, answer mechanism, and active/closed state.
IDEAL-057.reason: Ovis must build a prompt card without reading glyphs or footer hints.

IDEAL-058.predicate: Prompt answer atomically validates prompt version, liveness, session identity, answer schema, and authority, then returns accepted or a typed conflict without guessed key presses.
IDEAL-058.reason: A stale card must not answer a different prompt.

IDEAL-059.predicate: Open questions are independent records from turn execution state, so a working or completed turn can still have an unanswered question.
IDEAL-059.reason: Turn status alone cannot represent pending user input.

IDEAL-060.predicate: A queued first message is bound to launch ID, requesting principal, and declared readiness, with accepted, sent, cancelled, or expired state queryable.
IDEAL-060.reason: Startup must not type a task into an initialization dialog.

IDEAL-061.predicate: Multiline paste is encoded against the current bracketed-paste mode or rejected before delivery, and ordinary text is never promoted into control input.
IDEAL-061.reason: A composer insertion must not unexpectedly execute embedded lines or escapes.

IDEAL-062.predicate: Agent integrations can submit and answer typed in-process prompts without providing a terminal-key equivalent.
IDEAL-062.reason: A widget that accepts only extension events must remain usable from Ovis.

IDEAL-063.predicate: Turn waits bind to a specific send or turn ID and return completed, blocked, exited, lost, cancelled, or timeout without treating timeout as completion.
IDEAL-063.reason: Another turn or a background child must not satisfy the wrong wait.

IDEAL-064.predicate: Any authenticated program can register an arbitrary agent label and session reference without membership in a built-in brand list.
IDEAL-064.reason: New agents must have the same identity contract as known brands.

IDEAL-065.predicate: Agent lookup returns the registered record or explicit `agent: null` for a valid non-agent pane, reserving not-found for missing resources.
IDEAL-065.reason: A plain shell must not be an exceptional lookup failure.

IDEAL-066.predicate: Accepted sequenced status reports remain authoritative until replaced, cleared, or invalidated by their declared lifetime, never by screen or process-name heuristics.
IDEAL-066.reason: The runtime must not undo a program's report 200 ms later.

IDEAL-067.predicate: Status distinguishes working, idle, blocked, done, background, error, and unreported, with origin, session, sequence, and turn identity in both snapshots and events.
IDEAL-067.reason: Startup and live updates must tell the same story.

IDEAL-068.predicate: Stale or conflicting status reports return a typed rejection with current sequence instead of a success acknowledgement that hides non-application.
IDEAL-068.reason: A producer needs to know whether its report changed state.

IDEAL-069.predicate: A turn outcome and finish generation never change merely because a human focused, viewed, or acknowledged the pane.
IDEAL-069.reason: Completion is a fact independent of notification presentation.

IDEAL-070.predicate: Parent/child links, child status records, notification policy, and die-with-parent behavior are explicitly declared and do not relabel the parent's session.
IDEAL-070.reason: Delegation must not confuse provider-child activity with the orchestrator's turn.

IDEAL-071.predicate: Process inspection identifies shell, launcher, foreground and background processes with PID plus start token, or reports unsupported fields explicitly.
IDEAL-071.reason: Missing foreground evidence must not be mistaken for exit or PID continuity.

IDEAL-072.predicate: Session binding includes agent ID, process incarnation, source, reference kind and value, history identity, and revision, changing explicitly on resume or replacement.
IDEAL-072.reason: A transcript must not be selected by directory or recency alone.

IDEAL-073.predicate: Conversation reads and events provide typed user, assistant, tool-call, and tool-result records with stable IDs, ordering, and tool-call linkage.
IDEAL-073.reason: A common conversation surface must not confuse terminal menus with messages.

IDEAL-074.predicate: Message records preserve commentary versus final phase and all mixed text/tool-result content blocks.
IDEAL-074.reason: Progress and mixed provider records must not be dropped or misrepresented.

IDEAL-075.predicate: Conversation pagination cursors bind to history identity and revision, and detect append, truncation, replacement, and same-size rewrites.
IDEAL-075.reason: Cached history must not silently survive a changed underlying transcript.

IDEAL-076.predicate: Branch, fork, rewind, and resume records explicitly select the active history chain while retaining addressable off-branch records.
IDEAL-076.reason: Old abandoned ranges must not appear as part of the current conversation.

IDEAL-077.predicate: Turn records expose start and end boundaries, outcome and available timestamps, while model and reasoning metadata are nullable reported fields.
IDEAL-077.reason: Idle time and footer guesses must not inflate duration or invent metadata.

IDEAL-078.predicate: History listings are bounded, newest-first, and include title, timestamps, agent/session IDs, and typed resume references without following paths outside authorized stores.
IDEAL-078.reason: History discovery must be safe and independent of provider file layout.

IDEAL-079.predicate: Missing structured conversation or prompt support is advertised as unavailable with provenance, and any displayed terminal text remains explicitly terminal output.
IDEAL-079.reason: An unsupported agent must not produce fabricated chat records.

IDEAL-080.predicate: Local and remote resource addresses resolve through stable machine IDs and opaque resource IDs, with mutable display names unable to redirect an existing binding.
IDEAL-080.reason: Renaming or reconnecting a machine must not change the destination of queued work.

IDEAL-081.predicate: Remote transport authenticates the expected runtime, keeps protocol bytes separate from diagnostics, and returns typed authentication or trust failures.
IDEAL-081.reason: SSH banners and credential prompts must not corrupt the wire stream.

IDEAL-082.predicate: A lost remote line marks its resources unavailable with last-known revision and never silently omits them or falls back to a local target.
IDEAL-082.reason: The roster must distinguish unreachable resources from deleted ones.

IDEAL-083.predicate: Each machine has independent deadlines, cancellation, queues, and failure state, so a stalled remote cannot block local work or another machine.
IDEAL-083.reason: Cross-machine orchestration must remain responsive during partial outages.

IDEAL-084.predicate: Pane, tab, workspace, and split-node IDs survive layout moves, and structural mutations preserve each client's selection unless that client explicitly requests a focus change.
IDEAL-084.reason: Browser selection and automation must not yank a terminal user's focus.

IDEAL-085.predicate: Workspace/tab creation returns all created IDs and a separate agent-launch outcome, including resources left behind after partial failure.
IDEAL-085.reason: A failed agent launch must not hide a successfully created workspace.

IDEAL-086.predicate: Split, zoom, swap, resize, and ratio changes require explicit IDs and return resulting geometry, revision, and changed or no-op reason without silent clamping.
IDEAL-086.reason: Layout controls must have deterministic effects independent of focused panes.

IDEAL-087.predicate: Worktree operations accept explicit repository and checkout identities and return branch, source relationship, dirty/locked state, open workspaces, and operation outcome.
IDEAL-087.reason: Clients must not retry from a guessed source workspace.

IDEAL-088.predicate: Close and worktree-remove requests identify all affected resources and require explicit group or force scope before touching resources beyond the named target.
IDEAL-088.reason: A single-pane action must not unexpectedly close a linked group.

IDEAL-089.predicate: Templates are discoverable by stable name and version and launch through the same explicit argv, parent, readiness, and first-message contract as direct programs.
IDEAL-089.reason: Agents should select roles without embedding private launch conventions.

IDEAL-090.predicate: Plugin discovery returns identity, version, enabled state, action schema, applicable contexts, and an explicit unavailability reason for non-invocable actions.
IDEAL-090.reason: Ovis must not offer actions that the runtime will silently refuse.

IDEAL-091.predicate: Plugin invocation returns a durable run ID with queryable state, bounded output, truncation, exit result, and IDs of resources it created.
IDEAL-091.reason: Printed output must not be the only way to discover a plugin-created pane.

IDEAL-092.predicate: Remote orphan notifications are acknowledged and replayed after reconnect, and die-with-parent decisions use parent incarnation rather than a reused address.
IDEAL-092.reason: Network loss must not abandon declared child-lifecycle obligations.

IDEAL-093.predicate: PTY holders continue owning and draining programs through control-server crash, planned restart, client disconnect, and SSH logout on every supported platform.
IDEAL-093.reason: A frontend or transport lifetime must not become the program's lifetime.

IDEAL-094.predicate: Planned restart preserves program incarnations and terminal state, emits recovery boundaries, and returns explicit outcomes for interrupted operations and waits.
IDEAL-094.reason: Preserved processes must not imply preserved sockets or in-flight replies.

IDEAL-095.predicate: Crash recovery reports retained output ranges, any gaps, screen exactness, and new stream identities before restoring readiness.
IDEAL-095.reason: Recovered tail bytes must not be passed off as complete history.

IDEAL-096.predicate: After host reboot, persisted resources are listed as restored metadata or explicitly relaunched processes with new incarnations, never as surviving pre-reboot processes.
IDEAL-096.reason: Layout persistence is not process survival.

IDEAL-097.predicate: A durability acknowledgement is issued only after atomic state commit, and recovery exposes corrupted or unsupported records without silently replacing them with healthy-looking defaults.
IDEAL-097.reason: Acknowledged state must remain distinguishable from lost state.

IDEAL-098.predicate: `doc.get` returns value and version, while `doc.set` atomically compares version, commits a bounded value, and emits a revisioned change or typed conflict.
IDEAL-098.reason: Shared agent state needs compare-and-swap rather than last-writer-wins races.

IDEAL-099.predicate: Server stop, control-server restart, terminal kill, and metadata removal are distinct operations whose receipts enumerate affected process incarnations.
IDEAL-099.reason: An administrative verb must not hide whether programs were terminated.

IDEAL-100.predicate: Updates expose staged verification, activation, rollback outcome, and progress without replacing the active runtime on a failed integrity or compatibility check.
IDEAL-100.reason: Remote installation failure must leave an inspectable runnable state.

IDEAL-101.predicate: Retention limits for history, events, receipts, plugin runs, and finished terminals are advertised, and eviction advances a visible floor or tombstone rather than returning an empty success.
IDEAL-101.reason: Clients need to distinguish never-existing data from expired data.

IDEAL-102.predicate: Every connection has an authenticated principal and resource scope, with local endpoint permissions and remote credential validation enforced before access.
IDEAL-102.reason: A transport connection alone must not grant unrestricted machine authority.

IDEAL-103.predicate: Observe credentials cannot send input, answer prompts, resize, take over, launch, mutate documents, or change workspace state through any API or stream frame.
IDEAL-103.reason: Read-only behavior must hold beyond the Ovis UI.

IDEAL-104.predicate: Credentials are runtime-scoped, revocable, rotatable, and expiring, and revoked authority is rechecked before each mutation including queued writes.
IDEAL-104.reason: A previously authorized socket must not retain stale write rights.

IDEAL-105.predicate: Agent report authority is bound to a registered process/session and cannot overwrite another agent's identity, prompt, status, or conversation.
IDEAL-105.reason: Explicit reporting still needs an ownership boundary.

IDEAL-106.predicate: Prompt-answer and takeover permissions are checked independently of blocked status or possession of a terminal address.
IDEAL-106.reason: Blocked-state convenience must not substitute for access control.

IDEAL-107.predicate: Executable launches, paths, payload sizes, and remote operations are validated against typed schemas and caller scope without shell interpolation of protocol values.
IDEAL-107.reason: Structured requests must not become ambiguous remote shell commands.

IDEAL-108.predicate: Runtime diagnostics and audit records redact credentials and secret-input payloads, and stored terminal/history data obey explicit access and retention policy.
IDEAL-108.reason: Observability must not create a second unprotected copy of sensitive input.

IDEAL-109.predicate: Plugin actions and machine administration require explicit granted scopes and cannot inherit another client's lease or authority.
IDEAL-109.reason: Extension execution must respect the runtime's access boundary.

IDEAL-110.predicate: `--json` produces schema-defined output regardless of TTY state, with success on stdout, structured failure on stderr, and published stable exit codes.
IDEAL-110.reason: Scripts must not infer output mode from invocation environment.

IDEAL-111.predicate: CLI parse errors exit before connection, targetless automation returns `needs_target` with structured candidates, and help, schema, and skill commands do not start a daemon.
IDEAL-111.reason: Discovery and invalid commands must be safe to run unattended.

IDEAL-112.predicate: One versioned machine-readable schema defines requests, replies, events, errors, channels, limits, and capabilities with collision-free type names for generated clients.
IDEAL-112.reason: Ovis types must not drift from the runtime's actual contract.

IDEAL-113.predicate: Same-generation compatibility preserves existing methods and required outputs, permits optional additions, and documents tolerant handling of new output enum values.
IDEAL-113.reason: Additive runtime releases must not break existing clients.

IDEAL-114.predicate: The binary ships a version-matched `--skill` manual and schema, and every supported command and failure kind is discoverable without reading source.
IDEAL-114.reason: An agent must not depend on hidden flags or stale external instructions.

IDEAL-115.predicate: Structured logs correlate request, operation, principal, machine, runtime, resource, sequence, and outcome without mixing diagnostics into protocol stdout.
IDEAL-115.reason: Cross-machine failures need traceable evidence rather than attach-text parsing.

IDEAL-116.predicate: Health metrics expose active streams, per-consumer queue bytes, event lag, dropped/resynced ranges, RPC latency, and recovery state through read-only queries.
IDEAL-116.reason: Operators need to distinguish consumer backpressure from runtime failure.

IDEAL-117.predicate: Operation inspection distinguishes accepted, running, committed, failed, cancelled, and outcome-unknown states and exposes supporting receipts or process evidence.
IDEAL-117.reason: A success-shaped message must never be the only proof that work finished.

IDEAL-118.predicate: Attach and observe streams forward Kitty, iTerm2 and sixel graphics sequences byte-identical and whole, dropping an over-cap sequence entirely with a typed notice.
IDEAL-118.reason: Viewers render images; the runtime must neither corrupt nor split them.

IDEAL-119.predicate: A reattach replays every image whose placement is still on screen, in receipt order, and none that scrolled off, was cleared or was deleted.
IDEAL-119.reason: Reconnecting viewers see the same screen as continuous ones.

IDEAL-120.predicate: Screen reads and records mark image placements with a placeholder {image_id, format, rows, cols, bytes} and never inline payloads.
IDEAL-120.reason: Agents reason about layout without paying for pixels.

IDEAL-121.predicate: Graphics caps (per sequence, per terminal store) are advertised in hello as decimal strings and enforced through store entries sized to the cap; the daemon performs no decoding.
IDEAL-121.reason: Bounded memory and a stable trust boundary.
